documentation: docs/ci_cd.md -> 'Publish-blocking required checks'. This file is the ONE canonical, machine-consumed inventory of the repository-required product checks that must be successful, for the exact product SHA, under trusted workflow identity, before any mutable `latest` release, Docker image, or immutable version-tag artifact is published. .github/scripts/verify_publication_gate.py is the only consumer; .github/scripts/verify_required_ci.py proves the branch-protection required set, ci.yml's frozen `main-publish-gate` array, the `main-publication-required-checks` gate, and release.yml's `validate-release-sha` are set-equal to it by construction. Adding a required context without publication coverage fails policy CI.

required_checks.rationale: The publishing jobs live in this same workflow run and each declares `needs: test` plus `needs.test.result == 'success'`, so the aggregate is proven in-run rather than through the Actions API. The version-release verifier has no such in-run relationship and requires a successful push run of ci.yml for the exact tag target.

The workflow is itself a protected trusted-policy file that no pull request may edit, so it cannot be given a push trigger by an ordinary change. GitHub's merge queue lands its synthesized head commit on `main` verbatim, so the exact product SHA carries a `merge_group` run of this workflow on a `gh-readonly-queue/main/` branch. That run is matched by workflow id, canonical path, workflow name, event, queue-branch prefix, and head SHA; a commit pushed directly to `main` under an administrative bypass has no such evidence and therefore does not publish.
